data.raw_text:
My mother was a Short Mountain Tennessee Gunter girl, a true Mamma Grizzly when it came to her family. Mom was 17 years, 8 months, 7 days old when I was born. Dad met Mom after returning from WW2 serving in the Philippines. She was living in Ivy Bluff near to where Dad lived. Mom used to laugh she had to come off the mountain to find a husband as she and her sisters had whipped every boy on Short Mountain. 
     In the 60s Dad was building race cars to run in ARCA late model division and other local tracks. We had Fords and the 406 CI was the largest motor available at the time. In 1963 ½ Ford introduced the world to the 427 CI hands down better than the old 406, Dad surprised Mom with a brand new 1963 ½ Ford Galaxy 500, with the 427. Mom was thrilled, Mom had some hot rod in her it seems, she drove it back & too work and everywhere else she went. Dad worked on building a high power 390 and one week end dad told mom he needed to service her car so into the shop it went we had that beautiful 427 out in a jiffy and the 390 installed. The next day mom came home from work madder than a wet hen. She lined up Dad, Me and my Brother and demanded to know what we had done to her motor as it did not run as fast. After she calmed down and dad told mom about needing it for one of our race cars, she "Begrudgingly agreed". I doubt Dad had much marital bless for a while, but we had the 427. This would have been a good end to the story but now “the rest of the story’. I told you we installed that engine in record time, and the gas line did not get tightened enough and after a few days it came loose. Mom was at K-mart when the engine caught on fire after the fire department put it out we took it home to rebuild the engine and repair the car, mom was 10 times madder about that surprise. We were blessed mom was so tough as we three & my two sisters would have driven anyone else crazy. Many years later, in my 30s I told mom I was sorry for all the grief I had caused her through the years, Mom smiled at me and said Bobby I don’t remember any that was bad as you are a good son. Mom has been in Heaven for 15 years and I miss her every day, look forward to that great reunion as it is closer everyday. Bob
